characterization_methods.key_findings: For the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C reference, aging reduces UTS and TE; embrittlement is most apparent for 24 h aging above 500 °C.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements

characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness of the 0Al material is ~200 HBW (flat over 0-6 Al); aging slightly increases hardness.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm; XRD performed on the rolling plane

characterization_methods.key_findings: no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations; fully recrystallized microstructure with grain size ~20 μm and some retained Mn microsegregations
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction by grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques

analytical_models.equation_role: evolution of dislocation densities ρc, ρw, ρd during plastic deformation
analytical_models.model_name: dislocation density evolution model (cell interior, cell walls, dipoles)
analytical_models.model_note: extends the three-internal-variable model of Roters et al. with a physical description of twin nucleation (Steinmetz et al.).

parameters.name: n (average number of active slip systems)

analytical_models.equation_role: critical twinning stress and twin nucleation rate

computational_details.simulation_method: temperature-sensitive dislocation-density-based constitutive strain-hardening model for low-SFE fcc metals with mechanical twinning (three internal variables extended with a twin nucleation description)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: validated against experimental true stress-true strain and strain-hardening curves of a Fe-22wt.%Mn-0.6wt.%C model TWIP steel at seven temperatures (293-873 K), using one coherent parameter set

interfaces.slip_behavior: mechanical twinning (TWIP effect) prevails as the deformation mechanism; dislocation-based strain hardening is followed at higher loads by mechanical twinning

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: aging response: the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy weakens/embrittles with aging (YS virtually unchanged, hardness slightly increased, UTS and TE reduced), whereas the 8Al alloy strengthens with aging

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace; successively filled from a 4-kg ingot.
10 × 50 × 130 mm³-sized blocks hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.

processing_steps.method: cutting perpendicular to the rolling direction into segments
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: segments with dimensions 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Aging conducted at 450 °C, 500 °C, 550 °C, and 600 °C for 0 h, 1 h, and 24 h; this sample is the 600 °C / 24 h condition.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: all plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: tensile specimens cut perpendicular to the rolling direction from 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ segments

hardness.uncertainty: approximate value read from Fig. 3d, where hardness is flat at ~200 HBW over the 0-6 wt.% Al range (includes this 0Al sample)

yield_strength.uncertainty: value is the reported as-homogenized YS; the paper states aging of Fe-30Mn-1.2C leaves the YS virtually unchanged

structures.overall_structure: fully recrystallized single-phase austenitic (fcc γ) microstructure with grain size ~20 μm and some retained Mn microsegregations

unmapped_findings: Aging of the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy leaves the YS virtually unchanged but reduces UTS and TE; embrittlement becomes most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and higher temperatures (>500 °C), i.e., this 600 °C/24 h condition.
Aging increases the hardness of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy only slightly.

In Fig. 4, the Al-free 0Al 'T + t' (24 h aged) series follows a broad trend from about 490 MPa at ~8% elongation to about 800 MPa at ~70% elongation, indicating the spread of aged 0Al tensile behavior.
No κ-carbide (L′1₂) precipitation is reported for this Al-free sample; the κ-carbide APT/TEM analysis in Fig. 5 pertains to the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al alloy after 24 h at 600 °C, not this 0Al sample.

For context, the as-homogenized (unaged) reference Fe-30Mn-1.2C state has 360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, and 77% TE; these values are for a different (as-homogenized) sample, not this aged 600 °C/24 h sample.
